newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: More gas projects needed to exploit Asian reserves.
newsitem.headline: More gas projects needed to exploit Asian reserves.

text.p: Asia needs to improve radically the infrastructure for natural gas to exploit its huge reserves, a senior official of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) said on Thursday.
"Only about 15 percent of the proven gas reserves in Asia have been developed," Julian Payne, executive director of the ADB told the Asian Gas conference in Singapore.
He said infrastructure development was critically needed to exploit the reserves.
The ADB expected a major demand for investment in new gas pipelines in the next 15 years, but it was unlikely governments would be able to mobilize the funds, Payne said.
"The financing requirements are enormous," he said.
Payne said ADB estimated US$70 billion, equivalent to five billion dollars per year, may be needed over the next 15 years.
The ADB would use its funds in limited amounts to help encourage additional funds for projects from the private sector, he said.
Four percent of total ADB lending was for gas infrastructure projects, totalling more than $2 billion, he added.

Payne said there remained major question marks about how quickly infrastructure projects could move ahead, including geo-political stability and the role of the private sector in gas, which may be considered a strategic asset requiring government control in many countries.
